sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

- When working on pi topics, read the docs and examples, and follow .md cross-references before implementing
- Always read pi .md files completely and follow links to related docs (e.g., tui.md for TUI API details)

toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

# FUTO Keyboard

The goal is to make a good modern keyboard that stays offline and doesn't spy on you. This keyboard is a fork of [LatinIME, The Android Open-Source Keyboard](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/packages/inputmethods/LatinIME), with significant changes made to it.

Check out the [FUTO Keyboard website](https://keyboard.futo.tech/) for downloads and more information.

The code is licensed under the [FUTO Source First License 1.1](LICENSE.md).

## Issue tracking and contributing

Please check the GitHub repository to report issues: [https://github.com/futo-org/android-keyboard/](https://github.com/futo-org/android-keyboard/)

The source code is hosted on our [internal GitLab](https://gitlab.futo.org/keyboard/latinime) and mirrored to [GitHub](https://github.com/futo-org/android-keyboard/). As registration is closed on our internal GitLab, we use GitHub instead for issues and pull requests.

If you want to help translate the app, please do so via our Pontoon instance: https://i18n-keyboard.futo.org/

Due to custom license, pull requests to this repository require signing a [CLA](https://cla.futo.org/) which you can do after opening a PR. Contributions to the [layouts repo](https://github.com/futo-org/futo-keyboard-layouts) don't require CLA as they're Apache-2.0

Please do not submit AI-generated pull requests, as these tend to make the codebase more difficult to understand. Pull requests made with clear heavy use of AI may be closed without comment. Please also avoid using AI to write issues, and try to explain it in your own words instead.

## Layouts

If you want to contribute layouts, check out the [layouts repo](https://github.com/futo-org/futo-keyboard-layouts).

## Building

When cloning the repository, you must perform a recursive clone to fetch all dependencies:
```
git clone --recursive https://gitlab.futo.org/keyboard/latinime.git
```

If you forgot to specify recursive clone, use this to fetch submodules:
```
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

You can then open the project in Android Studio and build it that way, or use gradle commands:
```
./gradlew assembleUnstableDebug
./gradlew assembleStableRelease
```

## APK signing

For official FUTO Keyboard versions, you can verify the APK's signing key fingerprint for integrity.

content.text:
Agent of Empires (aoe) is a terminal session manager that uses tmux to help you manage and monitor AI coding agents like Claude Code and OpenCode.

Run without arguments to launch the TUI dashboard.

Usage: aoe [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  add         Add a new session
  agents      List supported agents and their install status
  init        Initialize .agent-of-empires/config.toml in a repository
  list        List all sessions
  ps          Show a substrate-agnostic runtime view of in-flight sessions (tmux agent panes and ACP structured-view workers), one row each
  logs        View the configured AoE log file with a pretty viewer
  log-level   Get or set the running daemon's log filter at runtime. Pass a bare level (debug/info/...) for the safe expansion, or `--filter <expr>` for raw EnvFilter syntax. `--get` prints the current filter. Changes are ephemeral and lost on daemon restart
  remove      Remove a session
  send        Send a message to a running agent session
  status      Show session status summary
  killall     Force-stop everything aoe is running: the serve daemon, all agent workers, and all aoe tmux sessions. Destructive and unprompted
  session     Manage session lifecycle (start, stop, attach, etc.)
  group       Manage groups for organizing sessions
  plugin      Manage plugins (list, info, enable, disable, install, update, uninstall)
  profile     Manage profiles (separate workspaces)
  project     Manage the project registry used by multi-repo session pickers
  sandbox     Inspect and reclaim per-session sandbox agent stores
  worktree    Manage git worktrees for parallel development
  tmux        tmux integration utilities
  sounds      Manage sound effects for agent state transitions
  theme       Manage color themes (list, export, customize)
  settings    Inspect resolved settings and their provenance
  cityhall    Export and apply the CityHall config bundle (settings + projects)
  telemetry   Manage anonymous opt-in usage telemetry
  mcp         Inspect the effective MCP server set (provenance, conflicts, drift)
  skill       Query and manage agent skills
  hooks       Let AoE write agent hooks into each agent's own config, for every agent and every profile
  serve       Start the aoe daemon: REST/WebSocket API, plus the web dashboard in builds that embed it
  url         Print the URL of a running `aoe serve` daemon
  acp         Manage the ACP structured-view workers (doctor, ps, logs, prompt, approve, ...)
  uninstall   Uninstall Agent of Empires
  update      Update aoe to the latest release
  migrate     Run pending data migrations now, showing progress. A sandboxed session moves its own agent store when it starts; use this to move every eligible store at once instead. Trashed and archived sessions are skipped; each moves when it is started, or restore or unarchive it and run this again
  completion  Generate shell completions
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -p, --profile <PROFILE>
          Profile to use (separate workspace with its own sessions). Commands that consume or create profile state require an existing profile: an unknown name is refused, not created (make one with `aoe profile create`). Profile-independent commands such as `list --all` and `serve --stop` ignore it
          
          [env: AGENT_OF_EMPIRES_PROFILE=]

      --daemon-url <DAEMON_URL>
          Attach to a remote agent daemon instead of using the local session list. Equivalent to setting `AOE_DAEMON_URL`; pair with `AOE_DAEMON_TOKEN` for the bearer token. The session list goes through a bearer-only client, so `AOE_DAEMON_PASSPHRASE` does not work here yet; it works for `aoe acp <verb>` against the same `AOE_DAEMON_URL`. Only meaningful at the no-subcommand `aoe` invocation (the TUI dashboard); ignored otherwise
          
          [env: AOE_DAEMON_URL=]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

content.text:
# Configuration

Pi supports user-level and project configuration. User-level configuration lives in the agent directory, which defaults to `~/.pi/agent`. Project configuration lives in `.pi` under the working directory and loads after [project trust](security.md#understand-project-trust) is granted. The only exception is `sessionDir`, which Pi reads before resolving trust so it can locate sessions.

In interactive mode, use `/settings` to change common preferences. For other options, ask Pi to update the configuration or edit the relevant files directly. Run `/reload` after manually changing settings, keybindings, instructions, or resources.

## Agent directory

The agent directory is shown as `<agent-dir>` below. Set its location with the `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` environment variable or the SDK's [`agentDir`](sdk.md) option.

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `<agent-dir>/settings.json` | User-level [settings](settings.md), including preferences, defaults, resource paths, and Pi package declarations. |
| `<agent-dir>/keybindings.json` | Custom terminal UI and application [keybindings](keybindings.md). |
| `<agent-dir>/mcp.json` | [MCP servers](mcp.md) available in every project. |
| `<agent-dir>/models.json` | [Compatible endpoints, models, and model overrides](models.md#configure-a-compatible-endpoint). |
| `<agent-dir>/auth.json` | Saved API keys and OAuth credentials. |
| `<agent-dir>/AGENTS.override.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `AGENTS.MD`, `CLAUDE.md`, or `CLAUDE.MD` | User instructions applied across working directories. |
| `<agent-dir>/SYSTEM.md` | Replaces Pi’s default system prompt. |
| `<agent-dir>/APPEND_SYSTEM.md` | Adds instructions to Pi’s system prompt. |
| `<agent-dir>/extensions/` | User [extensions](extensions.md). |
| `<agent-dir>/skills/` | User [skills](skills.md) and supporting files. |
| `<agent-dir>/prompts/` | User [prompt templates](prompt-templates.md) exposed as slash commands. |
| `<agent-dir>/themes/` | User [theme](themes.md) files. |

## Project `.pi` directory

| Path | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `.pi/settings.json` | Project-level [settings](settings.md), resource paths, and Pi package declarations. |
| `.pi/mcp.json` | Project [MCP servers](mcp.md). |
| `.pi/SYSTEM.md` | Replaces the system prompt for the project. |
| `.pi/APPEND_SYSTEM.md` | Adds project-specific instructions to the system prompt. |
| `.pi/extensions/` | Project extensions. |
| `.pi/skills/` | Project skills and supporting files. |
| `.pi/prompts/` | Project prompt templates exposed as slash commands. |
| `.pi/themes/` | Project theme files. |

For `SYSTEM.md` and `APPEND_SYSTEM.md`, the trusted project file takes precedence over the corresponding agent-directory file. Files with the same name are not combined.

## Context files

Context files are separate from project `.pi` configuration. Pi loads them from the agent directory, the working directory, and its parent directories. A context file applies whenever Pi runs in its directory or anywhere below it.

An `AGENTS.override.md` replaces `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` only in the same directory. It does not suppress context files from the agent directory or other directories.

Context-file discovery does not require project trust.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -x
cd /tmp
CLT=commandlinetools-linux-11076708_latest.zip
if [ ! -f "$CLT" ]; then
  curl -sSLo "$CLT" "https://dl.google.com/android/repository/$CLT"
fi
mkdir -p "$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools"
rm -rf "$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest"
unzip -qo "$CLT" -d "$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools"
mv "$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/cmdline-tools" "$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest"
SDKM="$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager"
yes | "$SDKM" --licenses > /tmp/licenses.log 2>&1
"$SDKM" --install "platform-tools" "platforms;android-35" "build-tools;35.0.0" "cmake;3.22.1" "ndk;28.2.13676358" > /tmp/sdk-install.log 2>&1
rc=$?
if [ $rc -ne 0 ]; then
  echo "exact NDK install failed, listing available ndk 28.2.x:" >> /tmp/sdk-install.log
  "$SDKM" --list 2>/dev/null | grep -i "ndk;28.2" >> /tmp/sdk-install.log
  # try a fallback exact version match
  FALLBACK=$("$SDKM" --list 2>/dev/null | grep -oP 'ndk;28\.2\.\d+' | sort -u | tail -1)
  echo "FALLBACK=$FALLBACK" >> /tmp/sdk-install.log
  if [ -n "$FALLBACK" ]; then
    yes | "$SDKM" --install "platform-tools" "platforms;android-35" "build-tools;35.0.0" "cmake;3.22.1" "$FALLBACK" >> /tmp/sdk-install.log 2>&1
  fi
fi
echo "SDK_INSTALL_DONE rc=$?" >> /tmp/sdk-install.log
ls "$ANDROID_HOME" >> /tmp/sdk-install.log

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Hardware-accelerated voice-input engine
#
# Self-contained build of whisper.cpp v1.9.3 (upstream, ggml monorepo)
# compiled into a single shared library "voiceinput_gpu". This is
# deliberately SEPARATE from FUTO's entangled pre-Vulkan ggml/whisper
# tree that is compiled into libjni_latinime.so: the CPU voice path is
# untouched and this library is only loaded by the app when the user
# enables hardware acceleration for a model.
#
# Acceleration backends (selected with VOICEINPUT_HW_ACCEL_BACKEND):
#   - vulkan  (default): ggml-vulkan, for Mali/other GPUs.
#   - hexagon (opt-in) : Qualcomm's official ggml-hexagon DSP/HTP backend
#                        (HVX/HMX), for Snapdragon/Adreno devices. Requires
#                        the proprietary Qualcomm Hexagon SDK and toolchain.
#
# Built only for arm64-v8a. 32-bit (armeabi-v7a) Android has effectively
# no Vulkan/DSP support worth shipping. Other ABIs keep building the CPU
# path as before.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.22)

if(NOT DEFINED ANDROID_ABI OR NOT ANDROID_ABI STREQUAL "arm64-v8a")
    message(STATUS "whisper-gpu: skipping (hardware engine is arm64-v8a only; ABI=${ANDROID_ABI})")
    return()
endif()

# Make host CMake packages (SPIRV-Headers etc.) findable even though the
# NDK toolchain restricts most find_* modes to its sysroot.
set(CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_PACKAGE BOTH)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Backend selection
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
set(VOICEINPUT_HW_ACCEL_BACKEND "vulkan" CACHE STRING
    "whisper-gpu: hardware acceleration backend (vulkan|hexagon)")
set_property(CACHE VOICEINPUT_HW_ACCEL_BACKEND PROPERTY STRINGS vulkan hexagon)

if(VOICEINPUT_HW_ACCEL_BACKEND STREQUAL "hexagon")
    # ggml-hexagon's CMake does message(FATAL_ERROR) if HEXAGON_SDK_ROOT is
    # missing; fail early with a clear message instead. HEXAGON_TOOLS_ROOT
    # may be derived automatically from the SDK's hexagon_sdk.json.
    if(NOT DEFINED HEXAGON_SDK_ROOT OR NOT IS_DIRECTORY "${HEXAGON_SDK_ROOT}")
        message(FATAL_ERROR
            "whisper-gpu: VOICEINPUT_HW_ACCEL_BACKEND=hexagon requires "
            "HEXAGON_SDK_ROOT to point at a Qualcomm Hexagon SDK installation")
    endif()
    set(GGML_HEXAGON ON  CACHE BOOL "ggml: enable Hexagon backend" FORCE)
    set(GGML_VULKAN  OFF CACHE BOOL "ggml: use Vulkan" FORCE)
    message(STATUS "whisper-gpu: backend = hexagon (HEXAGON_SDK_ROOT=${HEXAGON_SDK_ROOT})")
else()
    set(GGML_VULKAN  ON  CACHE BOOL "ggml: use Vulkan" FORCE)
    set(GGML_HEXAGON OFF CACHE BOOL "ggml: enable Hexagon backend" FORCE)
    message(STATUS "whisper-gpu: backend = vulkan")
endif()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Vulkan link-level fix (Android API levels) -- Vulkan backend only
#
# ggml-vulkan calls Vulkan 1.1 core functions (vkGetPhysicalDeviceFeatures2,
# vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties2, ...). The NDK's libvulkan.so stub only
# exports those from API level 28 (Android 9) onward; below that it exposes
# the Vulkan 1.0 surface only. This app's minSdk is 24, so AGP's
# find_library(Vulkan) resolves the API-24 stub and the final link fails with
# "undefined symbol: vkGetPhysicalDeviceFeatures2".
#
# The GPU engine is inherently for Vulkan-1.2-capable devices (API 29+), and
# its use is gated at runtime in Kotlin, so it is safe to link against the
# API-28 stub while the CPU path keeps supporting older devices. Pre-seed
# Vulkan_LIBRARY before ggml's find_package(Vulkan) runs (find_library does
# not re-search an already-cached variable).
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
if(GGML_VULKAN AND ANDROID)
    get_filename_component(_ndk_llvm_bin "${CMAKE_C_COMPILER}" DIRECTORY)  # .../llvm/prebuilt/<host>/bin
    get_filename_component(_ndk_prebuilt  "${_ndk_llvm_bin}" DIRECTORY)    # .../llvm/prebuilt/<host>
    if(NOT CMAKE_LIBRARY_ARCHITECTURE)
        set(CMAKE_LIBRARY_ARCHITECTURE "aarch64-linux-android")
    endif()
    set(_vk28 "${_ndk_prebuilt}/sysroot/usr/lib/${CMAKE_LIBRARY_ARCHITECTURE}/28/libvulkan.so")
    if(EXISTS "${_vk28}")
        set(Vulkan_LIBRARY "${_vk28}" CACHE FILEPATH "Vulkan library (API 28 stub for 1.1 symbols)" FORCE)
        message(STATUS "whisper-gpu: linking Vulkan against API-28 stub: ${_vk28}")
    else()
        message(WARNING "whisper-gpu: API-28 libvulkan stub not found at ${_vk28}; falling back to NDK default")
    endif()
endif()

# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# ggml options (upstream defaults are fine except what we pin here)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------
# BUILD_SHARED_LIBS is the real .so/.a switch for the ggml targets
# (GGML_STATIC only adds -static link flags for ggml's own tools).
# Force OFF so ggml-base/cpu/<accel> build as static archives and are
# linked into the single self-contained libvoiceinput_gpu.so.
set(BUILD_SHARED_LIBS        OFF CACHE BOOL "build shared libraries" FORCE)
set(GGML_STATIC              ON  CACHE BOOL "ggml: static link libraries" FORCE)
set(GGML_NATIVE              OFF CACHE BOOL "ggml: optimize the build for the current system" FORCE)
set(GGML_OPENMP              OFF CACHE BOOL "ggml: use OpenMP" FORCE)
set(GGML_CCACHE              OFF CACHE BOOL "ggml: use ccache if available" FORCE)
set(GGML_BUILD_TESTS         OFF CACHE BOOL "ggml: build tests" FORCE)
set(GGML_BUILD_EXAMPLES      OFF CACHE BOOL "ggml: build examples" FORCE)
set(GGML_BACKEND_DL          OFF CACHE BOOL "ggml: build backends as dynamic libraries" FORCE)
# Only the CPU + the selected acceleration backend are wanted; everything else stays off.
set(GGML_CUDA                OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(GGML_HIP                 OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(GGML_METAL               OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(GGML_SYCL                OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(GGML_VULKAN_RUN_TESTS    OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(GGML_VULKAN_VALIDATE     OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(GGML_VULKAN_DEBUG        OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)
set(GGML_VULKAN_MEMORY_DEBUG OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)

# ggml emits -Werror-style fatal warnings only if asked; it must never
# treat warnings as errors inside this project.
set(GGML_FATAL_WARNINGS OFF CACHE BOOL "" FORCE)

content.text:
# Building with Docker / Podman

This document describes how to build the **FUTO Keyboard** Android APK inside a
container, with no Android Studio and no Android SDK installed on the host.

It covers two approaches:

1. **[Self-contained Docker build](#approach-1-self-contained-docker-build)** —
   uses the repo's own `.ci/Dockerfile` (`gradle:8.14.3-jdk21`). Simplest, fully
   reproducible, nothing pre-built required.
2. **[Toolchain container + volumes](#approach-2-toolchain-container--volumes)** —
   a minimal image plus the SDK/NDK on a named volume. This is the setup used
   during development on this box (via Podman + distrobox). Faster rebuilds, SDK
   survives container recreation.

> The commands below show `docker`, but everything works identically with
> **Podman** (`podman`) and **distrobox**; just substitute the binary name.

---

## Prerequisites

| Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Disk | **~10 GB** free (SDK ~4 GB, NDK ~2 GB, Gradle caches ~2 GB, APK ~250 MB) |
| Network | Outbound access to `dl.google.com`, `services.gradle.org`, Maven Central, and GitHub |
| Container runtime | Docker **or** Podman |
| Git | With submodule support |

**Important — submodules.** The build depends on 7 git submodules (including
`libs/`, which carries the Mozc IME AAR and the QNN runtime AARs):

```bash
git clone --recursive <repo-url>
# or, if you already cloned without --recursive:
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

---

## Approach 1 — Self-contained Docker build

The repo ships a complete build image in `.ci/Dockerfile`
(`gradle:8.14.3-jdk21` + Android SDK 35 + NDK `28.2.13676358` + build tools +
AWS CLI). Build it and run the build in one shot:

```bash
# 1. Build the image (downloads the SDK + NDK; ~4 GB, takes a while)
docker build -t android-keyboard-ci -f .ci/Dockerfile .

# 2. Build the APK
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/workspace -w /workspace android-keyboard-ci \
  ./gradlew --no-daemon assembleUnstableDebug
```

The APK lands on your host at:

```
build/outputs/apk/unstable/debug/android-keyboard-unstable-debug.apk
```

> This approach compiles **everything**, including the hardware-acceleration
> engine (see [Hardware-acceleration engine](#hardware-acceleration-engine)),
> as long as the extra shader tooling is present in the image (the base
> `gradle:8.14.3-jdk21` image may need it added — see that section).

---

## Approach 2 — Toolchain container + volumes

The setup that was actually used during development. It keeps the **SDK/NDK on
a named volume** so you can recreate the container freely without re-downloading
~4 GB, and it separates the image (small) from the state (volume).

### 2.1 Image

Minimal base — Ubuntu 24.04 + JDK 17 + the few host tools the build needs. The
SDK is **not** baked in.

`android-toolchain/Dockerfile`:

```dockerfile
FROM docker.io/library/ubuntu:24.04

ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
ENV ANDROID_HOME=/opt/android-sdk
ENV PATH="$ANDROID_HOME/cmdline-tools/latest/bin:$ANDROID_HOME/platform-tools:$PATH"

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
        openjdk-17-jdk-headless \
        build-essential cmake ninja-build \
        unzip curl git ca-certificates \
        python3 file less \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* \
    && java -version 2>&1 | head -1

WORKDIR /workspace
```

> **JDK:** 17 or 21 both work (AGP 8.10.1 / Gradle 8.14.3 require ≥ 17).
> **`build-essential` / `cmake` / `ninja`** are required for the
> hardware-acceleration engine's shader compilation (see below).

Build it:

```bash
docker build -t android-toolchain:1 android-toolchain/
```

### 2.2 SDK/NDK volume

```bash
docker volume create android-sdk
docker volume create gradle-home

docker run --rm -it \
  -v android-sdk:/opt/android-sdk \
  android-toolchain:1 bash
```

Inside the container, bootstrap the SDK and install the exact versions this
project pins:

```bash
mkdir -p /opt/android-sdk/cmdline-tools
cd /opt/android-sdk
curl -o cli.zip https://dl.google.com/android/repository/commandlinetools-linux-13114758_latest.zip
unzip -q cli.zip && rm cli.zip
mv cmdline-tools latest && mkdir cmdline-tools && mv latest cmdline-tools

yes | /opt/android-sdk/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager --licenses
/opt/android-sdk/cmdline-tools/latest/bin/sdkmanager \
  "platform-tools" "platforms;android-35" "build-tools;35.0.0" \
  "cmake;3.22.1" "ndk;28.2.13676358"
```

### 2.3 Run the build

```bash
docker run --rm \

**⚠️ Needs device validation**

=== DEPLOYMENT ===
# Deploying Builds to the Test Phone (Syncthing)

This document describes how to get a freshly built APK (and its QNN model
package) onto the **Galaxy S23 Ultra** test device. Deployment is done by
dropping files into the **Syncthing** folder — the phone then receives them
automatically over the local network. No adb, no USB, no manual `scp` needed.

---

## The one rule that matters: the drop location

Syncthing runs **inside a podman container** (`systemd-syncthing`), and its
`/var/syncthing` is a **named volume** — *not* the host's `/var/syncthing`.

| Path | Is it watched by Syncthing? |
|---|---|
| `/var/syncthing/s23` (host) | ❌ **No.** This is a red herring — files here are invisible to Syncthing. |
| **`/var/lib/containers/storage/volumes/syncthing-data/_data/s23/`** | ✅ **Yes.** This is the real synced folder. |

**Always copy deployment artifacts here:**

```bash
/var/lib/containers/storage/volumes/syncthing-data/_data/s23/
```

### Why a volume?

The container's mounts are:

| Container path | Backed by |
|---|---|
| `/var/syncthing` | named volume `syncthing-data` (this is the synced folder) |
| `/syncthing` | bind mount of host `/home/gc/syncthing` (currently *not* used by the folder config) |

The `s23` folder config (`ss6ek-hhrv7`) points at `/var/syncthing/s23`, which
resolves to the volume. If you ever want to sync from the host home directory
instead, edit the container's `config.xml` to point the folder at
`/syncthing/s23` and restart the container — then `/home/gc/syncthing/s23/`
becomes the drop path.

---

## Step-by-step: deploy a fresh APK

### 1. Build the APK

From inside the toolchain container (distrobox `android-dbx`):

```bash
cd ~/android-keyboard
./gradlew assembleUnstableDebug
```

Output lands at:

```
~/android-keyboard/build/outputs/apk/unstable/debug/android-keyboard-unstable-debug.apk
```

### 2. Copy it into the synced folder

The volume's parent directories are root-owned, so use `sudo`:

```bash
sudo cp \
  /home/gc/android-keyboard/build/outputs/apk/unstable/debug/android-keyboard-unstable-debug.apk \
  /var/lib/containers/storage/volumes/syncthing-data/_data/s23/
```

### 3. Fix ownership so Syncthing can read it

Syncthing runs as `gc` inside the container. Make sure the file is readable
(and owned by `gc` for cleanliness):

```bash
sudo chown gc:gc \
  /var/lib/containers/storage/volumes/syncthing-data/_data/s23/android-keyboard-unstable-debug.apk
```

> ⚠️ `sudo cp` leaves the file owned by `root`. A `root`-owned file with mode
> `644` is still *readable* by Syncthing, but `chown` keeps things consistent
> and avoids permission surprises later.

### 4. Confirm Syncthing picked it up

Wait a few seconds (large files need hashing), then check the folder status:

```bash
sudo podman exec systemd-syncthing \
  sh -c 'curl -s http://localhost:8384/rest/db/status?folder=ss6ek-hhrv7 | grep -oE "\"(state|globalFiles|localFiles|inSyncFiles)\":[^,]+"'
```

You want to see:

```
"state":"idle"        (or "scanning" during the initial hash)
"globalFiles":3
"localFiles":3
"inSyncFiles":3
```

When `globalFiles == localFiles == inSyncFiles`, everything is indexed and
syncing to the phone.

### 5. Install on the phone

The file appears in the Syncthing folder on the S23 (inside Syncthing's
configured sync directory). Open it there and install — or move it to
`Downloads` via Termux first:

```bash
# On the phone (Termux), if you need it in Downloads:
termux-setup-storage        # once
cp ~/storage/<syncthing-dir>/android-keyboard-unstable-debug.apk ~/storage/downloads/
termux-open ~/storage/downloads/android-keyboard-unstable-debug.apk
```

## Hardware-acceleration engine

The repo vendors **whisper.cpp v1.9.3** (under `native/jni/src/whisper-gpu/`)
with its **Vulkan** backend, compiled into `libvoiceinput_gpu.so` (arm64-v8a
only). Its CMake step generates ~319 SPIR-V shaders **at build time**, which
requires extra host tooling **inside the container**:

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `glslc` (shaderc) | Compiles `.comp` → SPIR-V shaders |
| `SPIRV-Headers` | SPIR-V C++ headers consumed by ggml-vulkan |
| `g++` (`build-essential`) | Builds the host `vulkan-shaders-gen` tool |

> **glslc gotcha:** Ubuntu 24.04 does not ship a `glslc` binary package (only
> `libshaderc-dev`). Use a newer base (Ubuntu 26.04 / Debian trixie package it
> as `glslc`), or install a prebuilt `glslc` from the
> [shaderc releases](https://github.com/google/shaderc/releases). The Vulkan C
> headers/libs come from the NDK sysroot; `vulkan.hpp` + SPIR-V headers are
> vendored in `native/jni/src/whisper-gpu/third_party/`.

If the shader tooling is missing, the CMake configure step fails fast with a
`find_package(Vulkan COMPONENTS glslc)` error — install `glslc` and retry.

The QNN (Hexagon HTP) runtime for Snapdragon devices is pulled from Maven
(`com.qualcomm.qti:qnn-runtime`, `com.microsoft.onnxruntime:onnxruntime-android-qnn`)
and requires no build-time tooling beyond the NDK.

---

## Build commands & flavors

```bash
./gradlew assembleUnstableDebug      # default flavor, debug-signed, installable
./gradlew assembleStableDebug
./gradlew assembleStableRelease      # requires keystore.properties
./gradlew assemblePlaystoreRelease
```

| Flavor | `applicationId` | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `unstable` (default) | `org.futo.inputmethod.latin.unstable` | dev build |
| `stable` | `org.futo.inputmethod.latin` | release-track |
| `playstore` | `org.futo.inputmethod.latin.playstore` | Google Play |

**Signing:**
- **Debug** builds sign with the committed `java/shared.keystore` — no key setup
  needed, the APK installs directly.
- **Release** builds need a `keystore.properties` file (with `keyAlias`,
  `storePassword`, `storeFile`, `keyPassword`); without it the APK is produced
  unsigned.

The APK outputs follow the pattern
`build/outputs/apk/<flavor>/<debug|release>/android-keyboard-<flavor>-<debug|release>.apk`.

|---|---|---|
| Gradle | 8.14.3 | `gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties` |

| minSdk | 24 | `build.gradle` |

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
|---|---|
| `fatal: No names found` / missing `updateLocales` | Submodules not initialized — run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. |
| `Could not resolve ... :mozc-release:` | `libs/` submodule empty — init submodules. |
| `find_package(Vulkan COMPONENTS glslc)` fails | `glslc` not installed in the container — see [Hardware-acceleration engine](#hardware-acceleration-engine). |
| Gradle can't write to Gradle home | Volume ownership mismatch — chown the volume dir to the container user (`uid 1000`). |
| `undefined symbol: vkGetPhysicalDeviceFeatures2` at link | Linking against API-24 `libvulkan.so` stub; the wrapper already pins the API-28 stub — don't override `Vulkan_LIBRARY`. |

- The user transfers files to their Android phone with **Syncthing** (not ad-hoc HTTP servers, email, etc.).
- Syncthing runs as user `gc` in a rootless podman container (`syncthing.service`, image

Important: `languageSpecificModels` is empty in VoiceInputAction. So MultiModelRunner only uses primaryModel. The per-language model is resolved for the *first active locale* only. If the active locales are e.g. Lithuanian + English, `locale = locales.firstOrNull()`. The model chosen is for that locale. The primaryModel is the model assigned to the first locale (or built-in English fallback). If the user's active keyboard languages are English + Lithuanian, and English is first, the model is English-only -> Lithuanian fails. Or if Lithuanian is first but no Lithuanian model assigned, it falls back to built-in English (tiny.en) -> Lithuanian fails. Performance low -> tiny.en.

Also, `tryFindingVoiceInputModelForLocale` falls back to `BuiltInVoiceInputFallbacks[locale.language]` only for English; for other languages returns null unless a model is assigned. `resolveVoiceInputSelection` picks qnnModel if any and backend QNN etc. The settings UI per-language model assignment.

User says "when I load the model for different language, he seemed to fail and the performance is very low". Could be they imported a QNN model for Lithuanian? The QNN model is English-only (whisper_large_v3_turbo... is multilingual actually). Or they selected a multilingual ggml model for Lithuanian. Performance low could be because QNN fails and falls back to CPU? Let's investigate the QNN engine and model zip. The QNN model package is `REDACTED.zip`, likely multilingual large-v3-turbo. If QNN fails to load for a different language because the language token isn't in the model's vocab? Whisper large v3 turbo supports 99 languages; should be fine.

But "load the model for different language" may mean: in settings, for each language, assign a model. They loaded the QNN model for Lithuanian? Maybe the model import is tied to locale key; assigning a model under a different language doesn't update the active selection because of `findKeyForLocaleAndKind` key matching bug. Let's inspect `findKeyForLocaleAndKind` keysToTry: locale.toString(), locale.language, "${language}_${country.ifEmpty { language }}", lower/upper variants. If locale is `lt` (no country), keys:
- "lt"
- "lt"
- "lt_lt" (country empty -> language "lt")
- "lt_LT"
If the user imported the model under `lt_LT` or `lt`, one matches. If the model was imported under "lt-LT" (hyphen)? The keys use underscores. ImportResourceActivity likely stores key from locale.toString() which for Android Locale `lt_LT` is `lt_LT`, fine.

Maybe the model assignment UI uses the *display language* list, and for languages not supported by the model, the picker still allows. Hmm.

Let's read the GPU_QNN docs about per-language.

## Goal
1. Build the FUTO Keyboard APK from the `lithuanians` worktree and deliver it to the user's Android phone via their file-sharing setup.
2. Merge the `lithuanians` worktree with the GPU enablement branch (`qnn-longform` / `origin/GPUEnablement`) and fix any resulting build issues.
3. Rebuild the **container/build image** (`.ci/Dockerfile`) so it can compile the Vulkan/GPU engine — blocks on sandbox container-runtime limits, workaround documented.

## Constraints & Preferences
- File transfer to the phone must be via **Syncthing** (user: "I am using synching to share file with my phone … keep it in as a record?"). No ad-hoc HTTP servers/email.
- Syncthing layout: `syncthing-data` volume → `/var/syncthing` in container holds config + `s23` folder; published files go in `/var/lib/aoe/syncthing/s23`.
- Persistent environment notes must be recorded in `/var/lib/aoe/.config/onecli/pi_cli/pi-agent/AGENTS.md`.
- No sudo / root; container runs with "no new privileges".

## Progress
### Done
- [x] Installed Android SDK/NDK to `/var/lib/aoe/android-sdk` (`platform-tools`, `platforms;android-35`, `build-tools;35.0.0`, `cmake;3.22.1`, `ndk;28.2.13676358`); `local.properties` → `sdk.dir=/var/lib/aoe/android-sdk`.

- **Use Syncthing as delivery mechanism**: matches user's actual workflow; recorded in AGENTS.md.
- **Unset proxy env vars for Java/sdkmanager/Gradle**: sandbox proxies break downloads; direct connections work.
- **Install toolchains under `/var/lib/aoe/`**: no sudo.

Then "loading the model for a different language seems to fail and performance is very low". Could be because they assign a **QNN model** for Lithuanian. This is likely. The keyboard has active locales; voice action picks the first, not the current/primary language. There is no per-language switching. User says "when I load the model for different language, he seemed to fail and performance is very low" — perhaps they installed a Lithuanian model but the app still loads English because `getActiveLocales()` returns [en_US, lt_LT] or first is English. Since `languageSpecificModels` is always empty, no bail/switch. That perfectly explains "load the model for a different language" + "fails and low performance": it never uses the language-specific model.

### P10 [Low] Sanitizer + composing-wrapper can retype or delete the whole dictation
`ModelOutputSanitizer.sanitize` is computed against `inputTransaction.textContext` captured once at
window creation (`ActionInputTransactionIME.kt:78-81`), while partials have already been written
into the editor. With `VoiceInputAlternativeIC` default `true`, `setComposingText` is emulated via
`commitText` in `InputConnectionInternalComposingWrapper` (`:218-260`): if the final text is not a
strict extension of the last partial (capitalization change, trailing punctuation/space, dropped
`" you"`), the "Complex" branch backspaces `pastText.length - commonLength` and retypes everything —
for multi-KB dictations that is a full delete+retype of the accumulated text, and a wrong
`commonLength` can delete surrounding user text. `isAddition = text.startsWith(composingText)` is
also O(n) per partial on a string that grows with recording length.

### P11 [Low] Minor recording-loop issues
* `:377`, `:434`: `samples.sliceArray(0 until nRead).map { ... }.toFloatArray()` — two allocations
  + boxing-ish work per 100 ms read; a simple loop over `samples` is enough.
* `:387` RMS is computed over the whole 1600-sample array even when `nRead < 1600`, i.e. including
  stale samples from the previous block.
* `whisper_full` is called with `wparams.language = nullptr` (autodetect) when the keyboard has no
  selected language; on a `.en` model that is forced to `en` anyway, but with an English-only model
  plus a non-English keyboard language the forced language is silently ignored.

---

## 5. Recommended fix (design)

Do long-form in the app, not in one giant `whisper_full` call:

1. Split the recording into ≤30 s chunks (VAD-delimited where possible, fixed windows otherwise,
   0.5–1 s overlap, drop trailing overlap tokens).
2. Decode each chunk with `no_timestamps = true`, `audio_ctx` matched to the chunk length, so cost
   per chunk is bounded and memory stays flat regardless of total duration.
3. Concatenate chunk outputs; keep the existing sanitizer on the concatenated result.
4. Between chunks: report progress (`i/N`), honour cancel, and surface `res != 0` as a user-visible
   error instead of an empty result.
5. Independent of that: clear `partial_results` per inference, throttle partials, release the JNI
   float array, and use geometric buffer growth.

This also makes the whole "long-form" feature testable: each chunk is a normal <30 s inference.

---

## 6. Open questions / what is still needed

To confirm which of the above is the reported failure, the following is needed:

* Symptom: nothing inserted / capture stops at 30 s / capture stops ~2 s after a pause / wrong text
  / crash / frozen spinner.
* `logcat` filtered on `WhisperGGML`, `whisper_full`, `AudioRecord`, `AudioFlinger`, `ICPatched`.
* Whether `can_expand_space` and `use_vad_autostop` are default in the user's install
  (`settings` → voice input), and which model/backend is active.
* Device + Android version, and whether a Bluetooth mic is in use.

---

## 7. Backend comparison: is QNN also limited to 30 s?

Short answer: **yes, and harder than the CPU path** — the QNN/HTP engine is a *fixed-shape single
=== 250-275
**This matches the reported symptom exactly**: "audio longer than 30 seconds fails" on a QNN build
= you speak for a minute, the first 30 s appear, the rest is lost, and nothing indicates why.

### 7.2 QNN: second, independent cap — output tokens

`htp_whisper.cpp:42-43,394` → `WINDOW = 200`, `CACHE = 199`, decode loop `step < WINDOW - 1`, one
token per `Run`, input ids are the prompt during the first `promptLen` steps. Prompt is
`<|sot|> + <|lang|> + <|transcribe|> + <|notimestamps|>` (+ glossary tokens), so:

```
max content tokens per 30 s = 200 - promptLen  ≈ 196 (no glossary)
```

whisper.cpp allows up to 448 tokens per 30 s window. For dense speech this truncates mid-sentence,
and the margin is tighter for languages that need more BPE tokens per word (Lithuanian included),
and for long glossary/personal-dictionary prompts. Going past ~196 tokens would need a second
encoder pass, which the fixed KV cache (199 slots) cannot do.

### 7.3 QNN: no partial results, metrics unused

long QNN dictation completely opaque.

Snapdragon detection prefers `Build.SOC_MANUFACTURER` (API 31+) containing
`qualcomm`/`qti`, falling back to `ro.hardware`/`ro.product.board` code names
(`msm`, `sdm`, `sm8*`, `kalama`, `pineapple`, …). Mali detection covers
`mediatek`/`samsung`/`exynos`/`mt6*`/`s5e`/`mt8*`/`mt9*`.

A ggml model on a QNN backend (or a QNN backend that is not yet functional)
**falls back to CPU** — ggml cannot run on QNN and QNN cannot run ggml. A QNN
context binary on a non-QNN backend raises `GpuUnavailableException`, which the
recognizer maps to a dedicated `ModelLoadFailure.HardwareUnavailable` message
(`model_load_hw_unavailable`).

## Threading through the call chain

- `VoiceInputAction.loadSettings()` computes `preferHardware`
  (`getVoiceInputModelUseGpu || primaryModel is ModelQnnFileFile`) and resolves
  a `Backend` via `BackendSupport.resolveBackend`.
- `MultiModelRunConfiguration(backend = …)` (was `useGpu: Boolean`).
- `MultiModelRunner` → `ModelManager.obtainModel(model, backend)`, cache key
  `(modelKey, backend)`.
- `ModelLoader.loadGGML(context, backend)`.
- ggml loaders route `VULKAN` → GPU-with-CPU-fallback, everything else → CPU.
- `ModelQnnFileFile.loadGGML` routes `QNN` → `QnnWhisperEngine`, else throws.

# Voice input: review of the >30 s ("long-form") path

Branch/worktree: `lithuanians` @ `a0b84ef9a` (== `origin/master`)
Scope: built-in voice input (`voiceinput-shared` + `native/jni`). Sections 1-6 are the CPU/ggml
review; section 7 covers the QNN/HTP and Vulkan backends from `origin/GPUEnablement`
(`dc3a5d972`), which are **not** 30 s-limited in the same way.

---

## 1. TL;DR

* The 30 s boundary is **not** a model limit. It is the size of the recording buffer:
  `AudioRecognizer.floatSamples = FloatBuffer.allocate(16000 * 30)` (`AudioRecognizer.kt:110`).
* Long-form is enabled by `CAN_EXPAND_SPACE` (`"can_expand_space"`, `VoiceInputSettingKeys.kt:37`,
  **default `true`**) — surfaced in settings as "Long-form voice input". Each time the buffer runs
  out, another 30 s is appended (`AudioRecognizer.kt:299-309`). With the setting off, capture stops
  at 30 s by design.
* Native side: `audio_ctx` is derived from sample count and clamped to 1500
  (`org_futo_voiceinput_WhisperGGML.cpp:101`), and `no_timestamps` switches off above 25 s
  (`cpp:117`), which puts >25 s audio on whisper's multi-window timestamped path.
* **I could not make the GGML/whisper layer fail for long audio.** Built `whisper.cpp` from
  `native/jni/src/ggml` and ran it with the app's exact parameters and the bundled
  `tiny_en_acft_q8_0` model (see §3). 55 s of real speech decoded correctly into all 5 sentences.
* Therefore the reported "fails for audio longer than 30 seconds" is almost certainly **not** in the
  decoder. The realistic causes, in order of likelihood, are §4-P1 (latency + no cancel/progress),
  §4-P2 (errors swallowed), §4-P3 (`AudioRecord.read() <= 0` silently ends capture) and §4-P4
  (native leak that grows with audio length).
* **Exception — QNN/HTP (`origin/GPUEnablement`) is genuinely capped at 30 s.** The mel front end
  truncates the PCM to 48 000 samples and the encoder graph is a fixed `{1, 128, 3000}` input, with no
  chunking in Kotlin or native code. Recording >30 s there does not fail, it silently transcribes
  only the **first 30 s** (and the decoder is capped at ~196 output tokens). See §7.

---

## 2. What actually happens for a >30 s recording

Recording loop (`AudioRecognizer.recordingJob`, `AudioRecognizer.kt:311-445`):

| step | code | effect for long audio |
| --- | --- | --- |
| guard | `AudioRecognizer.kt:336` `remaining() < max(nRead,1600) && !expandSpaceIfAllowed()` | appends +30 s chunk (full copy) |
| VAD auto-stop | `:338` `hasTalked && numConsecutiveNonSpeech > 66` (≈2 s silence) | ends the recording, independent of the 30 s buffer |
| append | `:377` `floatSamples.put(...)` | `Short`→`Float`, per-sample `sliceArray`+`map` allocation |
| finish | `:339-346` / UI tap | `onFinishRecording()` (`:572`) |

Inference (`runModel`, `AudioRecognizer.kt:543-570`) → `MultiModelRunner.run` → `WhisperGGML.infer`
→ `WhisperGGML_infer` (JNI) → `whisper_full`, which walks the mel spectrogram window by window
(`seek_delta`) until `seek_end` (`whisper.cpp`, default `n_audio_ctx = 1500`).

So "long-form" = *one* `whisper_full` call over the whole recording, with
`audio_ctx = 1500`, `no_timestamps = false`, beam search 5.

---

## 3. Empirical verification (native path)

Harness: `/tmp/wtest` — `whisper.cpp`, `ggml.c`, `ggml-alloc.c`, `ggml-backend.c`, `ggml-quants.c`
from `native/jni/src/ggml`, linked against the shipped model
`voiceinput-shared/src/main/ml/tiny_en_acft_q8_0.bin.not.tflite`.
Parameters copied 1:1 from `org_futo_voiceinput_WhisperGGML.cpp`:
`max_tokens=256`, `audio_ctx = clamp(ceil(n/320)+32, 160, 1500)`, `temperature_inc=0`,
beam search 5, `suppress_blank=false`, `suppress_non_speech_tokens=true`,
`no_timestamps = n < 16000*25`, 4 threads.

| input | n_samples | audio_ctx | no_ts | res | segments | wall time (4 thr) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JFK sample 11 s, real speech | 176000 | 582 | 1 | 0 | 1 (correct) | 4.6 s |
| same clip ×5 = 55 s | 880000 | 1500 | 0 | 0 | 10 (5× correct) | 31.4 s |
| synthetic tone 45 s | 720000 | 1500 | 0 | 0 | 6 | 22 s |
| synthetic tone 120 s | 1920000 | 1500 | 0 | 0 | 26+ | 64 s |

Conclusions:

1. **No crash, no truncation, no `res != 0` for >30 s** — the full 55 s was transcribed, including
   the audio past the 30 s mark. The multi-window `seek_delta` loop works in this whisper version.
2. **Cost is linear in duration** and expensive: ≈0.5–0.6× realtime on a desktop with 4 threads.
   A mid-range phone with `n_threads` from `sysconf` (≤16, flag-only) will be 2–4× slower, i.e.
   ~2–4 s of decode per second of speech: 60 s dictation ⇒ 2–4 min of waiting.

Caveat: the tone tests were not speech, so they only prove the plumbing, not quality.
=== 225-250
Short answer: **yes, and harder than the CPU path** — the QNN/HTP engine is a *fixed-shape single
30 s window*: audio past 30 s is silently truncated. The Vulkan (ggml) engine is not, because it
keeps whisper.cpp's sliding-window loop.

| backend | entry point | long audio (>30 s) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CPU ggml (`master`) | `org_futo_voiceinput_WhisperGGML.cpp` | whole audio, whisper `seek_delta` loop, `audio_ctx` clamped to 1500 (§3: 55 s verified) |
| Vulkan ggml (`GPUEnablement`) | `native/jni/src/whisper-gpu/org_futo_voiceinput_WhisperGGMLGpu.cpp:277,291` | same `audio_ctx`/`no_timestamps` logic ⇒ same sliding-window behaviour |
| QNN/HTP (`GPUEnablement`) | `native/jni/src/qnn-htp/htp_whisper.cpp`, `whisper_mel.cpp` | **first 30 s only, silently** |

### 7.1 QNN: hard 30 s input cap, no chunking

* `QnnWhisperEngine.kt:20-22` says so explicitly: "The model is a single-shot 30-second window …
  [infer] pads/truncates its PCM to 30 s".
* `native/jni/src/qnn-htp/whisper_mel.cpp:23,27` → `SAMPLES_30S = 480000`, `N_FRAMES = 3000`.
* `whisper_mel.cpp:113` → `n = min(nSamples, SAMPLES_30S)` — everything past 30 s is dropped with
  **no log line, no error, no UI feedback**. The mel tensor is always `melBins * 3000`.
* `htp_whisper.cpp:272-285` → the encoder input is the fixed shape `{1, melBins, 3000}`; a mel array
  of any other length is rejected ("mel length mismatch"). There is exactly one encoder `Run()` per
  `nativeTranscribe`; there is no `seek`/window loop and no chunk concatenation anywhere.
* Recording side is unchanged by the branch (`AudioRecognizer.kt` on that branch is +14/−1 lines, all
  in the model-load failure path; `floatSamples`, `expandSpaceIfAllowed` and `CAN_EXPAND_SPACE` are
  byte-identical), so the user can record for minutes into `floatSamples` and the QNN engine then
  transcribes only the first 30 s of it.

**This matches the reported symptom exactly**: "audio longer than 30 seconds fails" on a QNN build
= you speak for a minute, the first 30 s appear, the rest is lost, and nothing indicates why.

# Hardware-Accelerated Voice Input — Review Recommendations

> **Purpose:** actionable, prioritized list of fixes and improvements for the
> hardware-acceleration change (`6141656bf`, "Add hardware-accelerated voice input
> (Vulkan + QNN/HTP)") on branch `GPUEnablement`.
>
> **Scope reviewed:** the ~128 authored files only (the 1277 vendored ggml /
> SPIR-V / ORT headers are excluded). Kotlin call chain + native bridges + build/UI.
>
> **Priority legend:** **P0** = functional bug, fix before shipping · **P1** =
> feature parity / UX · **P2** = native hygiene · **P3** = docs · **P4** =
> size / maintainability.
>
> **Status (2026-10-10):** all P0, P1 and P2 items below are addressed in the
> working tree on `GPUEnablement` and verified with `assembleUnstableDebug`
> (`BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, native libs recompiled + relinked). See the per-item
> notes. P3/P4 remain open.

---

## P0 — Correctness (fix first)

- [x] **1. Force the QNN backend for `ModelQnnZip`, not just `ModelQnnFileFile`.**
  - Where: `java/src/org/futo/inputmethod/latin/uix/actions/VoiceInputAction.kt:144-148`
  - Problem: `preferHardware = getVoiceInputModelUseGpu(...) || primaryModel is ModelQnnFileFile`.
    The working ZIP path returns `ModelQnnZip`, and `getVoiceInputModelUseGpu()`
    reads the **ggml `FileKind.VoiceInput`** pref key, which does not exist for a
    QNN-only user → `false` → `resolveBackend(..., false)` → `Backend.CPU` →
    `ModelQnnZip.loadGGML` throws `GpuUnavailableException`
    (`ModelData.kt:228-235`) → UI falsely reports "hardware unavailable".
  - Recommended change: add a `val requiresHardware: Boolean` (default `false`) to
    the `ModelLoader` interface, return `true` from `ModelQnnFileFile`/`ModelQnnZip`,
    and use `primaryModel.requiresHardware` in the `preferHardware` expression.

- [x] **2. Scope the import-failure handling to the QNN ZIP branch.**
  - Where: `java/src/org/futo/inputmethod/latin/uix/ImportResourceActivity.kt:927-1019`
  - Problem: `qnnZipImportFailed` is set by a `catch (e: Exception)` that wraps
    **all** import kinds, so a failed transformer / dictionary / ggml import shows
    the QNN-ZIP-specific string (`file_kind_qnn_zip_invalid`) and suppresses
    `GlobalIMEMessage.tryEmit(ReloadResources)`.
  - Recommended change: only set the QNN flag inside the `VoiceInputQnnZip` branch;
    show a generic error toast otherwise; keep emitting `ReloadResources` on
    non-QNN failures. Re-indent the block inside `withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {`.

- [x] **3. Reset the global whisper log callback on `close()`.**
  - Where: `native/jni/src/whisper-gpu/org_futo_voiceinput_WhisperGGMLGpu.cpp:134,164,342-349`
  - Problem: `whisper_log_set(log_capture, state)` sets ggml's **process-global**
    callback with `user_data = state`; `close()` does `delete state` without
    restoring it → any later log dereferences freed memory (use-after-free). With
    two GPU models loaded, the last `whisper_log_set` also wins, breaking the
    other engine's `last_error` classification.
  - Recommended change: call `whisper_log_set(nullptr, nullptr)` (or a stable
    router) in `close()`, and/or install the callback once at `JNI_OnLoad` with a
    live-state registry instead of a raw state pointer.

- [x] **4. Make the hardware gates ABI-aware (avoid `UnsatisfiedLinkError`).**
  - Where: `voiceinput-shared/.../ggml/GpuSupport.kt:22`, `BackendSupport.kt:78`,
    `voiceinput-shared/.../types/ModelData.kt:47-51`
  - Problem: both native engines are **arm64-v8a only**, but the gates check only
    device type / Vulkan version. An x86_64 emulator with Vulkan 1.2 → `VULKAN` →
    `System.loadLibrary("voiceinput_gpu")` → `UnsatisfiedLinkError`, which
    `loadGpuOrFallback` (catches only `GpuUnavailableException`) and
    `AudioRecognizer.preloadModels` (catches only the 3 typed exceptions) do not
    handle.
  - Recommended change: require `"arm64-v8a" in Build.SUPPORTED_ABIS` in the
    capability checks; also catch `LinkageError` in `loadGpuOrFallback` and wrap
    QNN construction so a missing lib surfaces as `GpuUnavailableException`.

---

- [x] **5. Decode long audio in overlapping chunks on the QNN backend (silent 30 s truncation).**
  - Where: `voiceinput-shared/.../ggml/QnnWhisperEngine.kt` (`infer`), new
    `voiceinput-shared/.../ggml/LongFormChunking.kt`, `native/jni/src/qnn-htp/htp_whisper.cpp`
    (`releaseCross`).
  - Problem: the HTP graph accepts exactly one 30 s window — `whisper_mel.cpp`
    clamps `nSamples` to `SAMPLES_30S` (480 000) and the encoder input is the fixed
    `{1, melBins, 3000}` tensor — so everything past 30 s was dropped with no log
    line and no UI feedback, while the recorder (long-form voice input) kept
    growing the buffer to minutes.
  - Change: `infer` plans 29 s windows with a 5 s overlap (`LongFormChunking.planChunks`),
    runs mel + encoder + greedy decode per window, and stitches the transcripts with
    `mergeOverlap`, which removes the words duplicated by the overlap (longest
    suffix/prefix word match, case- and punctuation-insensitive, CJK per character,
    capped at ~20 words). Recordings ≤ 29 s keep the old single-shot path exactly.
    One partial result is emitted per finished chunk (the HTP decoder cannot stream),
    and the encoder cross-attention caches are released after each window — the next
    encoder `Run` overwrote `h->cross` without freeing it, which also leaked one
    cross-cache set per dictation on a cached engine handle.
  - Remaining: the 200-slot decoder window (`WINDOW`/`CACHE`) still caps a chunk at
    ~196 tokens, so dense speech can be cut mid-sentence.

---

## P1 — Feature parity & UX

- [x] **6. Wire the glossary / prompt into the QNN decoder (or disable it explicitly).**
  - Where: `voiceinput-shared/.../ggml/QnnWhisperEngine.kt:130-161`
  - Problem: `buildPrompt(languages)` ignores the `prompt` argument, so the
    personal-dictionary glossary that the CPU path honours is silently dropped.
    `bailLanguages`, `decodingMode` (always greedy, not BeamSearch5) and
    `suppressNonSpeechTokens` are also ignored.
  - Recommended change: tokenize the glossary into the decoder prompt for QNN, or
    at minimum disable/annotate the glossary UI for QNN models so the gap is not
    silent.

- [x] **7. Resolve the single-file QNN loader.**
  - Where: `voiceinput-shared/.../types/ModelData.kt:199`
  - Problem: `QnnWhisperEngine(context, file, file)` uses the same file as both
    encoder and decoder session — almost certainly non-functional for a single
    graph. The doc comment at `ModelData.kt:175-177` ("throws on construction,
    blocked on `LessOrEqual`") is stale.
  - Recommended change: support an encoder+decoder pair for the legacy
    `FileKind.VoiceInputQnn` path, or remove `ModelQnnFileFile` /
    `FileKind.VoiceInputQnn` to shrink the surface.

- [x] **8. Fix the misleading hardware-acceleration switch on Snapdragon.**
  - Where: `java/src/.../settings/pages/Languages.kt:420`,
    `voiceinput-shared/.../ggml/BackendSupport.kt:78-88`
  - Problem: the toggle is shown whenever Vulkan ≥ 1.2 (Snapdragon qualifies), but
    Snapdragon always routes to QNN and a ggml model on QNN degrades to CPU — so
    the switch reads "faster transcription" yet does nothing.
  - Recommended change: hide the toggle where it cannot take effect, or show the
    resolved backend in the subtitle.

- [x] **9. Make `ModelManager` thread-safe.**
  - Where: `voiceinput-shared/.../whisper/ModelManager.kt:17-22` (+ `preload()` in
    `MultiModelRunner.kt`)
  - Problem: unsynchronized `HashMap` mutated by parallel `Dispatchers.Default`
    jobs (pre-existing, amplified by the new backend key).
  - Recommended change: `ConcurrentHashMap` + `computeIfAbsent`, or a `Mutex`.

---

## P2 — Native hygiene

- [x] **10. QNN decode-loop cleanups** (`native/jni/src/qnn-htp/htp_whisper.cpp`):
  - Release `outs` OrtValues on the mid-loop `check()` failure path (currently
    leaked).
  - `DeleteLocalRef` the `GetObjectArrayElement` references for languages/bail.
    (These are in the GPU bridge, `whisper-gpu/org_futo_voiceinput_WhisperGGMLGpu.cpp`
    `infer()`, not `htp_whisper.cpp`; fixed there.)
  - Guard `mel::init` global state against concurrent construction during
    `preload()`, or init the filterbank once.

---

## P3 — Documentation

- [ ] **10. Correct the drifted docs.**
  - Where: `GPU_QNN_INTEGRATION.md` still says the engine is an "honest skeleton"
    that throws on construction, that the ZIP holds `encoder.bin`/`decoder.bin`,
    and that detection reads 4 KB. Code is a working ORT loop, expects
    `encoder.onnx`/`decoder.onnx`, and reads up to 64 KB.
  - Also fix the stale comment at `ModelData.kt:175-177`, and the inventory counts
    in `GPU_FEATURE_WRAPUP.md` §4.1 (listed 17 files / +693-−83; actual 18 files /
    +1167-−82 for the non-vendored set).

---

## P4 — Size & maintainability

- [ ] **11. Use Maven coordinates for the QNN AARs.**
  - `com.microsoft.onnxruntime:onnxruntime-android-qnn:1.27.0` and
    `com.qualcomm.qti:qnn-runtime:2.48.0` are on Maven Central (confirmed in
    `GPU_QNN_INTEGRATION.md`). Removes ~76 MB of committed binaries from the `libs`
    submodule, improves provenance/licensing, and lets Gradle handle ABI filtering
    instead of hardcoded `implementation files('libs/...aar')`.

- [ ] **12. Attack APK/install size (currently ~248 MB).**
  - Enable ABI splits / App Bundle; note `useLegacyPackaging true` leaves native
    libs uncompressed on disk.
  - Consider on-demand model delivery (models are already large and per-arch).

- [ ] **13. Decide the Vulkan path's fate after a real Mali device test.**
  - If it doesn't pan out, dropping the Vulkan backend removes the ~51 MB
    `libvoiceinput_gpu.so` plus a large part of the vendored `whisper-gpu/ggml`
    tree. Otherwise narrow the vendored ggml source list or move it to a submodule.

- [ ] **14. Repo cleanup.**
  - Delete untracked `br.zip` (64 MB) and `.pod-sdk-install.log`.

package org.futo.voiceinput.shared.ggml

import android.os.Build

/**
 * Which Qualcomm chipsets the QNN (Hexagon HTP) voice engine can run on.
 *
 * A QNN graph is compiled for one Hexagon DSP architecture, so a Whisper build
 * only runs on the chipsets Qualcomm published that asset for. The allow-list
 * below is Qualcomm's own, taken from two files rather than guessed:
 *
 *  1. Which chipsets have Whisper assets at all — the release manifest of the
 *     model this engine targets (`precisions[*].chipset_assets` keys):
 *
 *       https://huggingface.co/qualcomm/Whisper-Large-V3-Turbo/raw/main/release_assets.json
 *
 *  2. Which Android SoC part number each chipset slug corresponds to — Qualcomm's
 *     device list, `chipsets[<slug>].aliases` (plus `htp_version` and `soc_model`),
 *     from the same AI Hub Models release:
 *
 *       https://github.com/quic/ai-hub-models/blob/v0.62.2/src/qai_hub_models/devices_and_chipsets.yaml
 *
 * Regenerating both after an upstream release (the second URL's part number is in
 * the `aliases` lists, upper-cased):
 *
 *   V=0.62.2
 *   curl -sSL -o release_assets.json \
 *     https://huggingface.co/qualcomm/Whisper-Large-V3-Turbo/raw/main/release_assets.json
 *   curl -sSL -o devices_and_chipsets.yaml \
 *     https://raw.githubusercontent.com/quic/ai-hub-models/v$V/src/qai_hub_models/devices_and_chipsets.yaml
 *   jq -r '.precisions[].chipset_assets | keys[]' release_assets.json | sort -u
 *
 * The manifest names AI Hub devices, never Android SoC strings, so the mapping to
 * a part number comes from column 2 — with one exception worth spelling out.
 * There is no `qualcomm-snapdragon-8gen2` entry in the manifest; the assets for
 * the Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 — the Galaxy S23 — are published under
 * `qualcomm-qcs8550-proxy`, AI Hub's stand-in device. That it really is the same
 * silicon is Qualcomm's own data: `qualcomm-qcs8550-proxy` and
 * `qualcomm-snapdragon-8gen2` both carry `soc_model: 43`, and the latter lists
 * `sm8550` as an alias with `reference_device: Samsung Galaxy S23`.
 *
 * Chipsets the manifest covers but Android cannot run on are deliberately absent
 * (`snapdragon-x-elite`, `snapdragon-x2-elite`: Windows-on-Snapdragon laptops, so
 * no Android device ever reports them). Chipsets Qualcomm supports on Android but
 * publishes no Whisper assets for are absent by construction — notably Snapdragon
 * 8+ Gen 1 (`sm8475`) and every 7-series — because there would be no model to run.
 *
 * Matching is by part number — [Build.SOC_MODEL] on Android 12+, falling back to
 * [Build.BOARD] / [Build.HARDWARE] for automotive boards that report the part
 * number there instead. Nothing but a part number is accepted, so a ROM that
 * reports only a marketing name or a platform code name is treated as
 * unsupported. That is the safe direction: the QNN option is hidden rather than
 * offered and then failing at load time. (Requiring Android 12+ costs nothing
 * here, since the oldest mobile chipset in the manifest is the 8 Gen 1, which
 * shipped with it.)
 */
object QnnSupport {

    /**
     * One chipset from Qualcomm's Whisper release manifest.
     *
     * @param aiHubId chipset slug, verbatim from the manifest, so the table can be
     *                diffed against it.
     * @param htpVersion Hexagon architecture, from `htp_version` in Qualcomm's
     *                device list. Used to check that this build packaged the
     *                matching `libQnnHtpV<N>Skel.so`.
     * @param socModels values [Build.SOC_MODEL] reports for devices on this
     *                chipset (upper-cased; matched ignoring Qualcomm's `-AB` /
     *                `-AC` / `-AD` part-number suffix).
     */
    private data class SupportedChipset(
        val aiHubId: String,
        val htpVersion: Int,
        val socModels: List<String>
    )

    /**
     * The chipsets with published Whisper-Large-V3-Turbo assets that an Android
     * device can actually be — mobile chipsets first, then automotive/IoT.
     *
     * The automotive/IoT entries only ship a `qnn_context_binary` rather than a
     * `precompiled_qnn_onnx` archive. That single-file kind is recognized by the
     * importer but cannot be loaded by the two-session engine (see
     * `ModelQnnFileFile`), so those entries are listed for completeness of
     * Qualcomm's manifest rather than because a runnable model exists for them
     * today; a device on one is treated as QNN-capable only once a
     * `precompiled_qnn_onnx` archive is assigned.
     */
    private val SUPPORTED_CHIPSETS = listOf(
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-snapdragon-8gen1", htpVersion = 69, socModels = listOf("SM8450")),
        // AI Hub's stand-in for Snapdragon 8 Gen 2 / SM8550 — see the note above.
        SupportedChipset(
            "qualcomm-qcs8550-proxy",
            htpVersion = 73,
            socModels = listOf("SM8550", "QCS8550")
        ),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-snapdragon-8gen3", htpVersion = 75, socModels = listOf("SM8650")),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-qcs9075", htpVersion = 73, socModels = listOf("QCS9075")),
        // `sm8750-ac` / `sm8850-ad`: Samsung's SKUs, reported as the base part
        // number once the suffix is stripped.
        SupportedChipset(
            "qualcomm-snapdragon-8-elite-for-galaxy",
            htpVersion = 79,
            socModels = listOf("SM8750")
        ),
        SupportedChipset(
            "qualcomm-snapdragon-8-elite-gen5-for-galaxy",
            htpVersion = 81,
            socModels = listOf("SM8850")
        ),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-qcs8275", htpVersion = 75, socModels = listOf("QCS8275")),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-sa7255p", htpVersion = 75, socModels = listOf("SA7255P")),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-sa8295p", htpVersion = 68, socModels = listOf("SA8295P")),
        SupportedChipset("qualcomm-sa8775p", htpVersion = 73, socModels = listOf("SA8775P"))
    )

    /**
     * Hexagon architecture of the matched chipset (`68`, `69`, `73`, `75`, `79`,
     * `81`), or `null` when the SoC is not one Qualcomm ships Whisper assets for.
     * [BackendSupport] treats a non-null value as "this chipset is supported" and
     * uses the number to confirm the matching `libQnnHtpV<N>Skel.so` made it into
     * this build.
     */
    fun matchedHtpVersion(): Int? = matchedSupportedChipset()?.htpVersion

    private fun matchedSupportedChipset(): SupportedChipset? {
        val candidates = reportedSocModels()
        if (candidates.isEmpty()) return null

        return SUPPORTED_CHIPSETS.firstOrNull { chipset ->
            chipset.socModels.any { it in candidates }
        }
    }

    /**
     * The part numbers this ROM reports, normalised: [Build.SOC_MODEL] first, then
     * [Build.BOARD] / [Build.HARDWARE] as a fallback for automotive boards that
     * report the part number there instead. Qualcomm's device list gives no
     * platform code names, so nothing but a part number is accepted — a device
     * whose ROM reports only a code name is treated as unsupported.
     */
    private fun reportedSocModels(): Set<String> {
        val raw = buildList {
            if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.S) {
                Build.SOC_MODEL?.let { add(it) }
            }
            Build.BOARD?.let { add(it) }
            Build.HARDWARE?.let { add(it) }
        }
        return raw.mapNotNull { normalizeSocModel(it) }.toSet()
    }

    /**
     * Upper-cases a ROM-supplied identifier and strips Qualcomm's part-number
     * suffix (`sm8550-ab` -> `SM8550`). Returns `null` for values that cannot be
     * a part number, so a marketing name such as `"Snapdragon 8 Gen 2"` is not
     * mistaken for one.
     */
    private fun normalizeSocModel(raw: String): String? {
        val normalized = raw.trim().substringBefore('-').uppercase()
        return normalized.takeIf { candidate ->
            candidate.length in 5..8 && candidate.all { it.isLetterOrDigit() }
        }
    }
}

content.text:
### 7.4 What is *not* limited

* Vulkan/ggml: `WhisperGGMLGpu.cpp:277` `audio_ctx = clamp(ceil(n/320)+32, 160, 1500)` and `:291`
  `no_timestamps = n < 16000*25`, identical to the CPU JNI, so long audio takes the multi-window
  path. `WhisperGGMLGpu.cpp:379` also **does** `ReleaseFloatArrayElements` — i.e. the JNI leak
  §4-P4 is already fixed on that branch, and only the CPU `org_futo_voiceinput_WhisperGGML.cpp`
  needs the one-line backport.

### 7.5 Options for QNN long-form

1. **Chunk in Kotlin, not native** (cheapest, no graph changes): split into ≤30 s segments with
   ~0.5-1 s overlap, call `QnnWhisperEngine.infer` per segment, concatenate, then de-duplicate the
   overlap. Also fixes the mid-sentence token cap, since each chunk gets its own 196-token budget;
   per-chunk progress/cancel becomes possible between segments. This mirrors the recommendation in §5
   and would work for every backend uniformly.
2. **Native chunking** inside `nativeTranscribe`: re-run the encoder per 30 s window and re-seed the
   KV cache per window (must reset `mask`/`selfKV`, and rebuild `cross` from the new encoder run).
   More efficient than (1) (no JNI/mel round-trip per chunk) but duplicates the loop that (1) gives
   you once, in the shared layer.
3. **Longer fixed shape**: export the QNN context binaries with e.g. a 60 s mel length. Doubles
   encoder cost/activation memory for every dictation, HTP memory is tight (large-v3-turbo w8a16),
   and it only moves the cliff to 60 s. Not recommended.
4. **Cap + be explicit**: if none of the above, clamp the recorded audio to 30 s whenever the QNN
   engine is selected (or refuse QNN for >30 s and fall back to the CPU engine) *and* tell the user.
   Silence is the worst of the options.

Recommended: (1) for the shared layer (it also subsumes §5 and helps CPU/GPU latency), plus the
`ReleaseFloatArrayElements` backport and a hard duration cap + user-visible message wherever a
backend cannot honour the audio length.

**Implemented** for QNN in branch `qnn-longform` @ `d4f5381c2` (worktree
`/var/lib/aoe/android-keyboard-worktrees/qnn-longform`, on top of `origin/GPUEnablement`):
`QnnWhisperEngine.infer` plans 29 s windows with a 5 s overlap (`LongFormChunking.planChunks`),
decodes each and stitches with `LongFormChunking.mergeOverlap` (word-level de-duplication,
fragment repair for words cut by a window boundary, CJK per character, ~20 word cap), emits one
partial result per chunk, and `htp_whisper.cpp` releases the per-window encoder cross-attention
caches (`releaseCross`) which would otherwise leak per chunk. Not runtime-tested: this machine has
no Android SDK/NDK/gradle, so the Kotlin and native changes are code-review-verified only; the
chunking + merge algorithms were validated against a line-by-line Python port (see the test table in
`/tmp/chunktest`), including a 10-minute / 25-chunk simulation with mid-word window cuts.

### 7.6 Verification status

Not yet exercised at runtime: the QNN engine needs a Qualcomm device with the AI Hub context
binaries and `libonnxruntime.so`, and the bundled `mel_filters_128.bin` / `whisper_vocab_v3.json`
assets (both are on the GPU branch, not in this worktree). The 30 s cap above is proven by code
reading (`min(nSamples, SAMPLES_30S)` and the fixed `{1, melBins, 3000}` tensor shape), not by a run.

summary:
## Goal
1. Build the FUTO Keyboard APK from the `lithuanians` worktree and deliver it to the user's Android phone via their file-sharing setup.
2. Merge the `lithuanians` worktree with the GPU enablement branch (`qnn-longform` / `origin/GPUEnablement`) and fix any resulting build issues.
3. Rebuild the **container/build image** (`.ci/Dockerfile`) so it can compile the Vulkan/GPU engine — blocks on sandbox container-runtime limits, workaround documented.
4. **NEW:** Investigate why loading a voice-input model for a *different* (non-English) language "seems to fail" and yields "very low" performance; inspect the code and identify the cause.

## Constraints & Preferences
- File transfer to the phone must be via **Syncthing** (user: "I am using synching to share file with my phone … keep it in as a record?"). No ad-hoc HTTP servers/email.
- Syncthing layout: `syncthing-data` volume → `/var/syncthing` in container holds config + `s23` folder; published files go in `/var/lib/aoe/syncthing/s23`.
- Persistent environment notes must be recorded in `/var/lib/aoe/.config/onecli/pi_cli/pi-agent/AGENTS.md`.
- No sudo / root; container runs with "no new privileges".

## Progress
### Done
- [x] Installed Android SDK/NDK to `/var/lib/aoe/android-sdk` (`platform-tools`, `platforms;android-35`, `build-tools;35.0.0`, `cmake;3.22.1`, `ndk;28.2.13676358`); `local.properties` → `sdk.dir=/var/lib/aoe/android-sdk`.
- [x] Installed full Temurin JDK 17 at `/var/lib/aoe/jdk/jdk-17.0.13+11` (system JRE lacks `javac` → "Toolchain installation … does not provide the required capabilities: [JAVA_COMPILER]").
- [x] Syncthing paths/permissions, Android build env, JDK/SDK locations, proxy caveat recorded in AGENTS.md.
- [x] Fast-forward merged `qnn-longform` → `lithuanians`; HEAD now `0b6e8a22c` (commit chain `0b6e8a22c → d4f5381c2 → dc3a5d972 → 6141656bf → a0b84ef9a`).
- [x] `libs` submodule re-pointed to `oozut/android-libs` `f71fba92`; AARs present (`libs/onnxruntime-android-qnn-1.27.0.aar` ~8.0 MB, `libs/qnn-runtime-2.48.0.aar` ~68.4 MB).
- [x] **First GPU build failed**: `> Task :buildCMakeDebug[arm64-v8a] FAILED`; `vulkan-shaders-gen` configure failed (no host `ninja`/`glslc`; stale `Vulkan_GLSLC_EXECUTABLE:FILEPATH=/bin/glslc`).
- [x] Diagnosed toolchain: SDK CMake ships `ninja` at `/var/lib/aoe/android-sdk/cmake/3.22.1/bin/ninja`; host `glslc` = `/usr/bin/glslc` (shaderc 2026.1); NDK glslc at `/var/lib/aoe/android-sdk/ndk/28.2.13676358/shader-tools/linux-x86_64/glslc`.
- [x] **Build succeeded** after prepending `$ANDROID_HOME/cmake/3.22.1/bin` and NDK shader-tools dir to PATH: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 3m 23s` (76 tasks; 22 executed).
- [x] APK verified: 247,268,384 bytes (236 MiB) at `build/outputs/apk/unstable/debug/lithuanians-unstable-debug.apk`; SHA-256 `fcd0bae305bc7007d88c81c93f3a2237313ab6a8f2182e85d07a90813233d399`; package `org.futo.inputmethod.latin.unstable`, versionCode `11758`, versionName `0.0.0-unstable`; `zipalign -c 4` → ZIPALIGN_OK.

  - `ModelData.kt`: `ModelQnnFileFile.loadGGML` throws `GpuUnavailableException` if backend != QNN **or** because a single context binary "cannot be split into encoder/decoder ONNX graphs"; `ModelQnnZip` requires `Backend.QNN`, loads `QnnWhisperEngine`.
  - `QnnWhisperEngine`: Whisper-Large-V3-Turbo w8a16, `MEL_BINS=128`, `SOT=50258`, `TRANSCRIBE=…`, v3 vocab; single-shot 30 s window; `d4f5381c2` added 29 s chunks + 5 s overlap (`LongFormChunking`).
  - `native/jni/src/qnn-htp/htp_whisper.cpp`: fixed-shape KV-cache decode, **`WINDOW=200` (199 cache + current), one token per Run**, `EOT=50257`, vocab 51866, `<|nospeech|>`=50363, 100 language tokens (50259..50358); decode loop `for (int step = 0; step < WINDOW - 1; step++)` → hard ~199-token cap per transcript chunk (likely truncation for verbose/non-English output).
  - `native/jni/org_futo_voiceinput_WhisperGGML.cpp`: `WhisperGGML_infer(env, instance, handle, samples_array, prompt, languages, bail_languages, decoding_mode, suppress_non_speech_tokens)`; `use_gpu=false` for CPU path.
  - `Language.kt` enum includes `Lithuanian`; `toWhisperString()` maps `lt`; whisper.cpp `g_lang` has `{ "lt", { 34, "lithuanian" } }` in both `ggml/whisper.cpp:289` and `whisper-gpu/whisper.cpp:315`.
  - Git archaeology: `ff29bf580 "Add resource importing (dict/voice/transformer)"` introduced `languageSpecificModels` (replacing `ENABLE_ENGLISH`/`ENABLE_MULTILINGUAL`/`*_MODEL_INDEX`/`LANGUAGE_TOGGLES`); `dc3a5d972` added per-language CPU/Vulkan/QNN picker via `ResourceHelper.resolveVoiceInputSelection()` and `ModelLoader.requiredBackend`; `4a9721abd "Initial multilingual typing implementation"` added `getMultilingualTypingLanguages` to subtype.

### In Progress
- [ ] Diagnosing root cause of "different-language model fails / low performance". Candidate causes identified but **none confirmed yet**: (a) `preload()` skip when ≥2 language models, (b) QNN HTP hard 199-token decode window truncating non-English output, (c) `verifyModelsExist()` hard-failing on any missing per-language model, (d) `ModelQnnFileFile` throwing `GpuUnavailableException` when it can't split, (e) per-locale backend pref key format mismatches.

### Blocked
- **Container image build blocked in sandbox**: `podman run docker.io/library/gradle:8.14.3-jdk21` → `Error: unable to copy from source … copy` (rootless `aoe` lacks `/etc/subuid`/`subgid`; lchown fails); `docker images` → `permission denied … /var/run/docker.sock`. Workaround: host `docker build -t android-keyboard-ci -f .ci/Dockerfile .`.

- **Use Syncthing as delivery mechanism**: matches user's workflow; recorded in AGENTS.md.
- **Unset proxy env vars for Java/sdkmanager/Gradle**: sandbox proxies break downloads.
- **Install toolchains under `/var/lib/aoe/`**: no sudo.

- **Investigating per-language model loading primarily through code reading + git history**, not device logs (no adb/journalctl access here).

sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>
